claims.head: Like for like: Formenton against Frost
claims.call: The Oilers’ L3 (Formenton, Michaels and Joseph) spends at least 38% of its 5-on-5 time against the Flames’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Oilers keep sending Formenton’s line (Formenton, Michaels and Joseph) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Babcock keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Flames’ third line is Suniev, Frost and Sharangovich.

claims.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
claims.body: On the power play, Edmonton is the league’s best, but Calgary is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Flames take could cost them. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 9 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 7th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Samuel Honzek is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Joel Hanley has not dressed for the last 7 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jake Middleton has taken his spot beside Zayne Parekh.
Connor Zary has not dressed for the last 6 games.
Jonathan Huberdeau is on injured reserve (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Ben Jones was added to the roster on Oct 21 and has played beside Joel Farabee and Matt Coronato.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, up from 2% last season.
Mattias Ekholm is out, reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin.
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins returned in their last game after missing 9 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 50% of the team’s power-play time in 10 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 2% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, down from 30% last season.

EDM.head: The Oilers should be in control
EDM.body: Even though Edmonton will be without Ekholm, the Oilers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. If the Flames want to spoil it, start with piling up shots.

CGY.head: A steep climb for the Flames
CGY.body: Even though Edmonton will be without Ekholm, the Oilers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Flames’ best hope is piling up shots, plus a big night in goal.

story.head: McDavid’s favorite opponent
paras: The Oilers have won three straight. The Flames have won two in a row.
At home, Mike Babcock likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Flames’ third line. The Oilers’ power play bites, but the Flames’ doesn’t.

items.text: Connor McDavid has a point in seven straight games against Calgary, and 15 points in his last nine against them.
The Flames have been without Samuel Honzek, Joel Hanley and Connor Zary for several games, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season.
The Oilers are newly without Mattias Ekholm, and have had to make do without Matt Savoie all season.
Leon Draisaitl has scored in five straight games.
